analysis.title: A much-needed comeback for Tech (Morning Line, 24 November 2026)
key_insights: Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO triggered a major equity turnaround, with Nvidia recovering as much as 31%. The Nasdaq rose 7% and the S&P 500 rose 4.7% in the session.
The tech sector had been under pressure despite strong Nvidia results and Anthropic's successful IPO, and regained ground on the unexpected CEO return.
Over a two-day swing Nvidia rose 8%, the Nasdaq 6.9% and the S&P 500 5%. The report calls it historic.
Risk appetite compressed bond spreads. The 10Y OAT-Bund spread narrowed nearly 7.5 bps to 150 bps and the BTP-Bund spread moved to about 105 bps.

OAT tightening began before the Huang news, driven by Macron's intention to enshrine a golden rule in the Constitution early next year. This needs Parliament convened in Congress and three-fifths of votes cast, and Marine Le Pen and other candidates have backed such a rule.
European equities rose: Euro Stoxx 50 +2.2%, DAX +2.2%, CAC +1.6%, FTSE 100 +1.4%. The Kospi gained 6% after the US tech correction.
The 10Y Bund yield fell below 3.30%. The dollar rebounded against all G10 currencies and EUR/USD fell to 1.088.
Credit rallied in high beta: iTraxx Main tightened 3 bps and Xover 15 bps, while euro IG corporate spreads tightened only 1 bp.
November composite PMIs: France fell from 46.6 to 46.2, euro area unchanged at 51.7, Germany rose from 53.4 to 55, Japan fell from 52.1 to 51.5.
Sanofi announced the acquisition of Insmed at $175 per share in cash, total consideration €37.6bn. Leverage is expected to rise well above the downgrade thresholds of 2.25x (Moody's) and 2.0x (S&P).
Merlin Properties now owns 100% of Forestalia's 240 MW data center project and plans to invest €2.5bn. Forestalia is seeking €150-300mn for power plants.
Scope Ratings says fuel costs are widening credit gaps among European airlines and accelerating consolidation. Pressure could intensify in 2027 as pre-conflict fuel hedges expire.
Day ahead: German Ifo (10:00), ECB Vujčić speech (12:00), US Conference Board Consumer Confidence (16:00).

market_movers.rationale: Shares recovered as much as 31% and rose 8% over two days after Jensen Huang's return as CEO was announced.
Sanofi's $175 per share Insmed deal (€37.6bn) is expected to push leverage above rating downgrade thresholds.

sector_views.rationale: Tech staged a comeback led by Nvidia after pressure despite strong results and Anthropic's IPO.

Yields fell, though risk appetite improved.

risk_factors: The golden rule requires a three-fifths majority in Congress and could fail.
Sanofi leverage could trigger rating downgrades.
Fuel costs and hedge expiries in 2027 pressure smaller European airlines.
US chip controls hitting ASEAN data center buildout.

iTraxx Xover at 311 bp, down 11.2 on the day. iTraxx Main at 63 bp.
geopolitical: Macron plans a constitutional golden rule on fiscal policy, requiring three-fifths of Parliament in Congress.
Scope notes pre-conflict fuel hedges expiring in 2027 for European airlines.
ASEAN data center boom hit by US chip controls, per research highlight list.
